newsitem.title: BELGIUM: US's Drazek tries to speed up EU veterinary talks.
newsitem.headline: US's Drazek tries to speed up EU veterinary talks.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman's trade adviser Paul Drazek will stay in Brussels until Friday to speed up negotiations for an agreement on the mutual recognition of veterinary standards, U.S. offficials said.
Washington is concerned that an estimated $2.0 billion trade in veterinary and phytosanitary products could be disrupted when the EU harmonises import rules on January 1, 1997.
"We are desperate for an agreement. The downside is almost beyond imagination," one official said, adding technical talks were continuing on Wednesday.

Imports of U.S. petfood and other meat products could be blocked due to stricter EU controls against Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) while shipments of other products would be subject of closer inspection, delay and extra cost.
Referring to the first day of talks with the European Commission on Tuesday the official said, "We did not get an agreement. Nothing was resolved."
The official added that Drazek would on Thursday bring up other farm trade issues, notably rice and malting barley.
The U.S. is pressing the EU to introduce a cumulative recovery system to allow traders to claw back excess rice import duties.

It is also impatient at EU delay in fixing rules for the import 38,000 tonnes of milled rice and 8,000 tonnes of brown rice duty-free to compensate U.S. exporters for trade losses after EU enlargement in 1995.

The EU has also still to introduce a 30,000 tonnes a year duty-free malting barley quota agreed as compensation for U.S. trade losses after the three new EU member countries -- Austria, Sweden and Finland -- raised duties to EU levels.
The head of the European Commission team, Corrado Pirzio-Biroli, said earlier that views of both sides had been clarified but there were still problems.

Unless significant progress were made in the veterinary talks before the end of 1996 there was little chance of EU member states agreeing to extend current import arrangements pending final agreement, he added.
